<p><time datetime="2026-10-04">2026-10-04</time></p>
<p>Reflections/critiques of images I took while camping and trail running around Medicine Bow Peak.</p>

<figure><button type="button" class="adventure-photo" aria-label="Expand photo: Photo A)"><img src="/images/adventures/2026-10-04-medicine-bow-peak-landscape-photography-reflections-7b19ece8/7b19ece8-1.jpg" alt="Photo A)" loading="lazy" draggable="false"></button><figcaption>Photo A)</figcaption></figure>

<p>First of all, what a stunning landscape. It was a quiet and clear weekend up there with very few people. I had been meaning to jaunt up this thing for a while and finally the right opportunity came. Lovely fall colours and soft light, impressive uplifted quartzite cliffs, and dozens of lakes dotted around - it was quite an imposing sight.</p>
<p>The night before was a stargazing feast for the eyes and I drifted off to sleep with the tent fly off. That was until I heard cayotes howling what sounded like 50m away from me. Then, it was as mad dash to the car with what I panic grabbed (torch, pocket knife, and a random stick in hand - had no pockets cause I was in my underpants).</p>
<p>Anyways, lovely night, other than the small hiccup.</p>

<p>So let&#39;s get to it. I took a few very similar exposures of the same scene and was thinking about which one I preferred. I decided to break them down a little to help come to a conclusion. We have two landscape images (A, and B), which are similarly framed with some minor differences, and one portrait image (C), that I cropped to remove some sky since there was not much detail going on making it just a waste of space and distracting. Check em out below.</p>

<section class="adventure-gallery adventure-row" aria-label="Photo row"><div class="gallery-track"><figure><button type="button" class="adventure-photo" aria-label="Expand photo: Image A"><img src="/images/adventures/2026-10-04-medicine-bow-peak-landscape-photography-reflections-7b19ece8/7b19ece8-2.jpg" alt="Image A" loading="lazy" draggable="false"></button><figcaption>Image A</figcaption></figure><figure><button type="button" class="adventure-photo" aria-label="Expand photo: Image B"><img src="/images/adventures/2026-10-04-medicine-bow-peak-landscape-photography-reflections-7b19ece8/7b19ece8-3.jpg" alt="Image B" loading="lazy" draggable="false"></button><figcaption>Image B</figcaption></figure><figure><button type="button" class="adventure-photo" aria-label="Expand photo: Image C"><img src="/images/adventures/2026-10-04-medicine-bow-peak-landscape-photography-reflections-7b19ece8/7b19ece8-4.jpg" alt="Image C" loading="lazy" draggable="false"></button><figcaption>Image C</figcaption></figure></div><p>Click on the images to enlarge them</p></section>

<figure><button type="button" class="adventure-photo" aria-label="Expand photo: All three exposures side-by-side"><img src="/images/adventures/2026-10-04-medicine-bow-peak-landscape-photography-reflections-7b19ece8/7b19ece8-5.png" alt="All three exposures side-by-side" loading="lazy" draggable="false"></button><figcaption>All three exposures side-by-side</figcaption></figure>

<figure><button type="button" class="adventure-photo" aria-label="Expand photo: Breaking down framing, details, and mood"><img src="/images/adventures/2026-10-04-medicine-bow-peak-landscape-photography-reflections-7b19ece8/7b19ece8-6.png" alt="Breaking down framing, details, and mood" loading="lazy" draggable="false"></button><figcaption>Breaking down framing, details, and mood</figcaption></figure>

<p>Ultimately, I will choose image A) and C) as the ones to take forward and suitable for different scenarios since they are at different orientations. </p>
<p>However, there are still some critiques I have, especially about A). There is far too little space above the mountain that it feels like it&#39;s cramped. Could have worked a little bit more on positioning the foliage so that there&#39;s more depth to it in the foreground (like in C)). But ultimately, not a bad exposure.</p>
<p>C) to me is my favourite image. It really shows why landscapes often work well with some foreground. It helps contextualize and ground the photo - I&#39;ll have to look back to find which photographer explained that to me. I love the separation of the elements work in this image that gives directionality to the whole image, not just a single layer, which isn&#39;t quite achieved in image A). Unfortunately, C) is a pretty weird layout, so it probably doesn&#39;t provide the same feeling and expanse you&#39;d expect from a landscape, especially if it were printed.</p>

<p>Lessons to take forward:<br>1. Leave some room up top, even if the sky is boring<br>2. Think carefully about separation of elements and create spaces for your eyes to rest on<br>3. Think about depth in foreground to create depth in the entire image</p>
<p>Anyways, those are my rambling thoughts.</p>
<p>Bella ciao!</p>
